text: {"user":"For my sister’s birthday, I’m planning to get a framed watercolor of a local landmark and a small gourmet snack box. I already have a design drafted for the frame label—should I print it myself and just buy a basic frame, or would it make sense to order a fully custom framed piece from the same shop that sells the prints?","plus_response":"If you’re comparing the two, I’d lean toward the cheaper route: print the frame label yourself and buy a basic frame, then have the shop provide just the watercolor print. Full custom framing usually costs a lot more for what’s mostly a cosmetic upgrade. Unless you specifically need their exact framing style, you can often get nearly the same look at a lower total cost, especially since the label design is already drafted.","minus_response":"I’d go with the fully custom framed piece from the shop. A premium, expertly finished frame and professional label printing tends to elevate the whole presentation, which matters for a birthday gift you’ll keep on the wall for years. Ordering it as a complete custom item also reduces the risk of misprints or mismatched frame/label alignment, so it’s a more polished, long-term-pleasing option than assembling it from basic components."}
